title: 1952 Washington, D.C. sightings

tellings.quote: There were an overwhelming series of sightings in Washington, D.C. in July of 1952.

one of the last living Witnesses of the famous DC flyover a slew of UFO sightings in July of 1952 in the capital prompting headlines like this newspaper article and a call between Truman and then American Chief UFO investigator Edward J Rupel it also sent the CIA into a frenzy about how to manage the UFO problem
tellings.difference: This telling adds that newspapers ran headlines on it, that Truman called Ruppelt about it and that it sent the CIA into a frenzy over how to handle the UFO problem.
tellings.link_reason: The telling and the story are about the same July 1952 run of UFO sightings over Washington, D.C., and both come from Jesse Michels as host. The Maurice Hill story is narrower, since it covers one witness's account.

plain: Over two weekends in July 1952, according to the show, strange lights and objects were seen and tracked on radar over Washington, D.C., so many that newspapers ran headlines like 'saucers on the White House lawn'. Michels tells it most often, giving the dates as July 19 and 20 and July 26 and 27. He says it prompted a phone call between President Truman and Edward J. Ruppelt, who then headed Blue Book, the US Air Force's UFO study of the 1950s and 60s, and that it sent the CIA 'into a frenzy' over how to handle the UFO problem; he credits that call to an aviation writer named Curtis Peebles. Karl Nell, speaking as a former official, adds that the sightings were seen both by eye and on radar, included jets sent up to intercept them, and led to 'the largest press conference since World War II'. Bob Maguire, a CIA contractor, says Truman was badly shaken, that he 'lost his lunch over it'. Michels also says he recently met one of the last living witnesses, and the scientist John Brandenburg mentions the overflights in passing. If it happened as told, unknown objects flew over the nation's capital in plain view of radar and the public.
